snapshot.title: Haptic, the AI guide that lives in your product
headings: How is Haptic different from a chatbot or a product tour?
How do I add Haptic to my product?
text: The AI guide that lives in your product. People say what they want to do, and Haptic points to exactly where to click, step by step.
No tours to script or maintain. Haptic reads the page as it is right now and points to the control that gets the job done.
During setup, Haptic reads your site and your help docs, so its directions match how your product really works.
Haptic reads the names of buttons and fields. What people type stays in the browser, and emails and long numbers are masked before anything is sent.
You pay for guides that finish. If someone stops, gets lost, or Haptic cannot find the way, that guide is free.
Free
1,000 finished guides a month.
For the first companies in, while we set Haptic up with you.
a month
1,000 finished guides a month, then $0.12 each.
For one product.
5,000 finished guides a month, then $0.08 each.
For several products, with staging sites.
Custom
Volume by agreement.
For larger rollouts. Tell us what your security and compliance teams need, and we will say plainly what we support today.
A guide is finished when the visitor uses the last control Haptic pointed at, or reaches the screen they asked for.
Haptic is free during early access, and billing starts after it. Every guide we count will be listed in your dashboard, so you can check the bill.
Prices are in US dollars and may change before general release.
A chatbot answers in text and leaves people to find the button themselves. A product tour plays the same fixed steps for everyone. Haptic works on the live pag…
© 2026 Haptic Labs

snapshot.title: Privacy, Haptic
text: Privacy
Last updated November 15, 2026
Haptic Labs makes Haptic. This page says what we collect on this website, and what Haptic reads when it runs inside a product.
We do not use analytics, advertising or tracking cookies on this site.
If you request access, we keep what you put in the form so we can reply. That is your name, work email and company, and anything you add about your product. A…
If you sign in, we keep your email address, your name if you give one, and the company you belong to, so you can reach your dashboard. Signing in sets cookies…
When you add a site, we read its public pages the way a visitor would, to learn what your product calls things. We do not sign in to anything and we do not sen…
When someone asks Haptic for help, it reads the page they are on. That means the names of buttons, links and fields, where each link leads, whether a box is ti…
Haptic does not read what people type into fields, or anything inside an area the page marks as one they write in, and it takes no pictures of the page. Two ki…
In what it reads, in the page's address and in the question itself, Haptic masks most email addresses, phone numbers and long numbers before anything leaves th…
Haptic is an AI guide and can be wrong, so check anything that matters before relying on it. To work out the next step, the question, that description of the p…
We keep the question that was asked, what Haptic said, the names of the controls it pointed at and where on the page they sit, which page of the product each s…
Haptic does not ask who a visitor is. But a name that shows on the page, in its address or on a control can be in what we keep, along with the time of each ste…
From a visit where nobody asks Haptic anything, we keep nothing about the visitor. For each web address the script loads on, we keep when it was first and last…
Our server uses a visitor's network address to limit how fast they can ask. Where a company also limits how much each visitor can ask in a day, a scrambled for…
We keep the record of each guide until the company asks us to delete it. Nothing deletes it on a schedule yet: a person at Haptic Labs does it on request. We d…
Progress through a guide is kept in the browser for that tab, and is cleared when the tab closes.
Questions, or want your details removed. Write to .
© 2026 Haptic Labs

snapshot.title: Haptic, the AI guide that lives in your product
headings: How is Haptic different from a chatbot or a product tour?
How do I add Haptic to my product?
text: The AI guide that lives in your product. People say what they want to do, and Haptic points to exactly where to click, step by step.
No tours to script or maintain. Haptic reads the page as it is right now and points to the control that gets the job done.
During setup, Haptic reads your site and your help docs, so its directions match how your product really works.
Haptic reads the names of buttons and fields. What people type stays in the browser, and emails and long numbers are masked before anything is sent.
You pay for guides that finish. If someone stops, gets lost, or Haptic cannot find the way, that guide is free.
Free
1,000 finished guides a month.
For the first companies in, while we set Haptic up with you.
a month
1,000 finished guides a month, then $0.12 each.
For one product.
5,000 finished guides a month, then $0.08 each.
For several products, with staging sites.
Custom
Volume by agreement.
For larger rollouts. Tell us what your security and compliance teams need, and we will say plainly what we support today.
A guide is finished when the visitor uses the last control Haptic pointed at, or reaches the screen they asked for.
Haptic is free during early access, and billing starts after it. Every guide we count will be listed in your dashboard, so you can check the bill.
Prices are in US dollars and may change before general release.
